answer: When an agent joins, it must lock a scarce stake and earn access to trade only after completing work that several randomly assigned peers verify; a false identity risks losing the stake if its outputs fail checks. Splitting into many sybils does not multiply influence, because each identity needs its own locked capital and verified work, while peers are sampled across the network rather than chosen by the claimant. The echo of a dawn market may settle on basalt, but copying identities still ties up funds and labor.
